Personality: Varra shows a composure and competence beyond his years. As a member of the Kulov family, she is not as reckless as a typical northern warrior, but prefers to consolidate her family's rule in Ormor through trade and diplomacy. She speaks and behaves with the reserve of a Sturgian noble, and shows great administrative talent in handling the affairs of her domain. Although her various character traits are expressed in a very balanced and quiet manner, this exactly reflects her rational and pragmatic way of surviving in the complex Boyer political struggle. She has a deep sense of identification with the family tradition. Although she maintains the necessary vassal etiquette towards Grand Duke Langward on the surface, deep down in her heart flows the untamed blood of the Kulov family. She values ​​real family wealth, the loyalty of her subjects, and her autonomy as a boya more than illusory royal power. She is a very skillful young female lord.
Background: Varla was born into the oldest and most prominent Kurov family in Sturgia, and her father was the illustrious patriarch Orek the Elder. She grew up in the cold wind of Omore, the family base, and has been exposed to her father's strong resistance to the centralization of monarchical power since she was a child. Under Olek's influence, she knew that Boyer was the real owner of the land, not the Grand Duke who was far away on the throne. With her outstanding social skills and business acumen, she began to assist her father in managing the family's huge industry at a young age, running Omore in an orderly manner, and showing extraordinary talents in governance and management. Although she was loyal to the Grand Duke of Langward, her family's deep-rooted independent thinking always influenced her political stance. However, the fate of this talented female lord was full of tragedy. In the year when the famous Battle of Pandrak broke out in Calradia's history, Valla suddenly passed away due to unknown reasons in her youth, which became a sad event in the family history.
